review: Independent read-only review of four CE2031 personal-probe native crashes

scope.inputs: Downloaded private crash logs, exact local unstripped F9 binary and matching source/generated bindings; prior observation of the crashing probe expression.

conclusion.confirmed_fault_site: All four actual Current thread / Thread 1 fault stacks share caller PC 0x00490700, in PythonBindings::xbmcgui_XBMCAddon_xbmcgui_ControlList_selectItem. This PC immediately follows an indirect virtual call through the native ControlList object's vtable.
conclusion.confirmed_source_defect: The observed crashing probe kept directory_control = xbmcgui.Window(10025).getControl(50) from a temporary Window wrapper, then called directory_control.selectItem(0). Exact F9 getControl bindings do not acquire a native reference for the returned Python holder. Disposing the temporary Window clears its sole owning native control reference, leaving the holder's pSelf dangling. The next virtual method dispatch therefore uses a freed ControlList object.
conclusion.confidence: High-confidence probe-induced use-after-free explanation: exact source ownership chain and exact instruction/caller correspondence agree with all four random/null fault targets. The logs alone do not contain allocation/free history or per-attempt deployed script hashes.
conclusion.missing_result_explanation: A native fatal signal bypasses Python except/finally and can prevent result.json from being written. Missing result.json alone was not used as proof of this diagnosis.
conclusion.signal_correction: Three crashes are SIGSEGV. The 20:09:23 crash is SIGBUS, not SIGSEGV.

common_backtrace_limit: Backtrace stopped: previous frame identical to this frame (corrupt stack?)

instructions: 0x004905c8: cmp r2, r3 ; compare with expected target 0x00520a24
symbol_evidence.line_resolution_limit: addr2line resolves exact function names; optimized/LTO binary does not provide a useful source line for these addresses. Generated source was checked separately.

source_chain.source: tools/ce_personal_smoke_remote.py:103-104 in observed crashing working version
source_chain.evidence: directory_control = xbmcgui.Window(10025).getControl(50); next statement directory_control.selectItem(0). No retained Window variable. The main agent has since replaced this path in the working file; current file hashes are not claimed as hashes of the crashing deployment.

getControl delegates to GetControlById. List/wraplist/fixedlist/panel native containers get a new ControlList wrapper. vecControls.emplace_back(pControl) owns a native Ref; the method returns a raw pointer. Repeated calls on the same retained Window can return its cached wrapper.
Window_getControl transforms apiResult with makePythonInstance(apiResult,true), without prepareForReturn or native Acquire.

prepareForReturn performs native Acquire/registration but is absent from getControl. makePythonInstance stores pSelf and optionally Py_INCREFs the Python holder only. PyHolder has no owner field. Window cleanForDealloc calls dispose before Release.

Window constructor returns makePythonInstance(apiResult,pytype,false); Window Python deallocation invokes cleanForDealloc. The temporary Window is therefore not kept alive by an extra Python reference from its constructor.

Native refs start at zero. vecControls' Ref acquires one. Window.dispose clears control fields and vecControls even for existingWindow=true. Its final Release reaches zero and deletes the ControlList; a returned Python holder has acquired no native reference.

Generated selectItem retrieves pSelf and invokes a virtual method. Actual ControlList::selectItem constructs GUI_MSG_ITEM_SELECT from parent/control IDs and sends it; it does not directly dereference pGUIControl. The observed invalid indirect target is consistent with the wrapper object being freed before method entry.

recommendations: Do not rerun the crashing temporary-Window/getControl/selectItem probe.
For this smoke test, prefer normal GUI input actions with item-identity and selection receipts; do not treat absence of a result file as an invitation to retry.
Holding a Window owner would address this specific temporary-owner lifetime gap, but is not device validation or a reason to immediately retest after a crash cascade.
Do not classify all native controls as inherently unsafe: this defect is specifically the returned wrapper's missing ownership across Window disposal.
Keep recovery and future device tests under the main agent/user's explicit coordination; this review authorizes no device writes or native patch.
